main_text.p: ita Luna per menfem id agit. Quod ita fit non accesfu, difcesfuq;, fed alterum increscente luce, alterum decrescente: tum enim tempus est frigidius & humidius. Hæc philosophus, quibus plenam Lunam, beneficio Solis, à quo lucem & uim calefaciendi, ipsa fortitur (semper enim semel in menfe Sol & Luna coeunt) hæc inferiora calefa-cere, uegetare abundè satis docemur. Quā-obrem ad omnes generationes perfectio-nesq; ipsam conducere ibidem Aristoteles confirmat. Propterea singulis plenilunij gammari Cancri, & cætera testacea sunt pleniora, non quòd ipsis maiorem alimo-niam, tu ipsa Luna suppeditet (nihil enim corporibus, in quæ agit, de sua substantia tribuit) sed quòd exanguium animalium cru-dos humores suo tepore concoquat, perfi-ciatq;. Crustata enim ac testacea ab aqua suum dutaxat sumunt alimentum. Quamuis autem istorum animalium humores [?]incrementa, & decrementa Lunæ ita moueantur, non propterea tamen cæterorum animalium sanguine præditorum humores Lunæ mutationibus esse obnoxios co-sequens est. Illa enim Lunam sive plenam, sive silentem fugere nequeunt: quandoquidem

page.notes: The scan's reading of the "p" after "humores" is doubtful and may be a printed sign; marked [?]. The word "quandoquidem" is split across the last line and the catchword "dem", which I have placed in the bottom margin, not in the text. Printed hyphens at line ends are kept (Quā-, calefa-, perfectio-, co-, alimo-, cru-, perfi-). The page number reads as 65 with an old-style 5. The printed words "plenilunij" and the stray mark after it are not transcribed as text. The printed letters "incref-" were read as "increscente" with the printed hyphen.
